doc.title: Hal Espinosa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 20, 2024

title: Woody's band breaks up; Covington's Dorsey band, Buddy Morrow and drummers
summary: Hal left Woody, played with Warren Covington's Tommy Dorsey band, returned to split lead with Bill Chase, then joined Buddy Morrow at $175.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: time, playing music that at the time I said if this is all I did the rest of my life — play this music — that’s all I’d ever want to do because the music was so much fun. I never played lead although the first time I was on Woody’s band I was playing like I said on one of the ends, Don was on the other end. And then Woody broke the band up because they just didn’t have any takers for booking the band at that time, so they disbanded the band. Bill Chase and Woody stayed on and they had a little quintet. And I went with the old Tommy Dorsey band when Warren Covington had it. So I did that for about, I don’t even remember, maybe five, six months. And then Woody got the band together again. He had tours happening. So I went back. This time I played split lead with Bill Chase. And so that’s the closest I got to playing lead with Woody. But Bill was a very good lead player, knew how to lay back, and swing, and there would be times when I’d play his part for about four bars starting to go up the register so I could take the mouthpiece off of its lip so you can start back down from a high G going up. So it was fun for me and fun, I’m sure, for him. Then after that I ended up getting a call from this guy, a tenor sax player called — I think his name was Bob McCoy. And he was a contractor for Buddy Morrow’s band. And Buddy was looking for a lead player and they were going to offer me $175 a week if I would take it. And I thought $175, I’m making I think it was $150 then. So I took it. And then after I left that’s when Sal Nistico came on the band and — I can’t think of the drummer — the brain, you know, as you get older things start hiding in your head. All the old memories.

But Jimmy Campbell was the drummer the whole time I was on Woody’s band until I left and that’s when he left and then Jake Hanna came in. So — and then Phil Wilson came in too I think. Jimmy went — left probably just after I did.
